# HunarLens — Training-Partition EDA Summary & Plot Interpretations (`eda_interpretations.md`)

**Reference:** [PROJECT_PLAN.md](file:///d:/Hunarlens/PROJECT_PLAN.md) §7 · **Generated by:** [scripts/run_eda.py](file:///d:/Hunarlens/scripts/run_eda.py)  
**Denominator & Scope:** Strictly restricted to the **70% PSU-disjoint training partition (`n = 17,913` eligible youth aged 15–24 in the labour force across `1,260` PSUs)**. Validation and test partitions were never accessed.

---

## 1. Class Counts and Proportions (`reports/figures/01_class_balance.png`)
* **Denominator:** `17,913` eligible youth in the training split (`10,167` Employed `[0]`, `7,746` Unemployed `[1]`).
* **Interpretation:** Positive-class (`is_unemployed = 1`) prevalence is `43.24%` unweighted (`43.34%` survey-weighted). Because employed youth outnumber unemployed youth, a majority-class dummy baseline predicts `0` everywhere and achieves `F1 = 0.00`, motivating our use of both the all-positive baseline (`F1 = 2p / (1 + p)`) and Average Precision (`AP`).

## 2. Missingness by Feature (`reports/figures/02_feature_missingness.png`)
* **Denominator:** `17,913` training observations across all 15 approved pre-encoding predictors.
* **Interpretation:** Core demographic, roster, and Census 2023 features exhibit complete coverage in the cleaned cohort (`max missing = 0.00%`). Nevertheless, the scikit-learn inference pipeline retains fold-local median imputation for numerics and explicit `"Unknown"` imputation + `OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")` to safely handle missing or unseen inputs at deployment time.

## 3. Numeric Distributions (`reports/figures/03_numeric_distributions.png`)
* **Denominator:** `17,913` training observations.
* **Interpretation:**
  * `age`: Mean `19.527`, median `20.0` (bounded `[15, 24]`, skew `-0.017`).
  * `household_size`: Mean `6.16`, median `6.0` (right-skewed `0.478`, reflecting multi-generational Pakistani households).
  * `household_dependency_ratio`: Mean `1.081`, median `0.75` (skew `2.309`).
  * `regional_pop_density_log1p`: Log1p transformation compresses the high-density Islamabad outlier (`2,609.12` persons/sq. km vs. Balochistan `42.90`).

## 4. Boxplots and Quantile Diagnostics (`reports/figures/04_numeric_boxplots_outliers.png`)
* **Denominator:** `17,913` training observations grouped by `Employed (0)` vs. `Unemployed (1)`.
* **Interpretation:** Large households (`P95 = 11.0`) and high dependency ratios represent genuine demographic structures in KP, Balochistan, and rural areas rather than data entry errors; per §7, plausible large households and dense regions are retained rather than deleted.

## 5. Numeric Correlation Heatmap (`reports/figures/05_numeric_correlation_heatmap.png`)
* **Denominator:** `17,913` training observations across the 6 numeric predictors and binary target.
* **Interpretation:** Linear correlations with `is_unemployed` are modest (`regional_urban_share`: `-0.053`, `household_dependency_ratio`: `+0.039`), confirming that youth unemployment vulnerability depends strongly on categorical human-capital and regional interactions rather than a single linear numeric proxy.

## 6. Education & Enrolment vs. Unemployment (`reports/figures/06_education_enrolment_vs_unemployment.png`)
* **Denominator:** `17,913` training observations, with all displayed bars meeting the `n >= 30` small-cell rule.
* **Interpretation:** Consistent with PBS LFS 2024–25 empirical findings, youth holding `Degree & Postgraduate` and `Intermediate` credentials face substantially higher descriptive unemployment rates during their initial labour-market transition than youth with `No Formal Education` (who are more frequently absorbed into informal/subsistence work). **Limitation:** These are cross-sectional descriptive associations conditional on labour-force participation, **not causal effects** of education.

## 7. Province, Locality, Sex & Descriptive Vocational Training (`reports/figures/07_province_locality_sex_training_summary.png`)
* **Denominator:** `17,913` training observations (`n >= 30` per cell).
* **Interpretation:** Urban youth and female youth in the labour force experience higher unemployment rates across provinces, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Islamabad exhibiting the highest regional pressure. Panel C illustrates why `vocational_training_status` is excluded from the predictive classifier (§5.3): `On-the-Job Training` occurs by definition among employed workers (`0.0%` unemployed), which would introduce severe post-outcome leakage if used as a predictor.
